title: Measure: count pairs, not paths

questions.prompt: In a stack of n pairs, both parts of each pair point to the pair below. How many times does the path-counting version meet a pair?

choices.why: That is the number of pairs. It is what your version should report, not what path counting does.
The doubling happens at every level, not once: each pair is reached twice as often as the one above it.
One meeting with the top pair, two with the next, four with the next: 1 + 2 + 4 + … with n terms.

checklist.step: Count each pair once, by identity, even around a cycle
Show the count growing by one for each new pair

hints: Two different questions: how many pairs exist, and how many ways there are to reach them.
Lists cannot go in a set, but id(pair) can, and it is the same number only for the same object.
Keep a set of ids and a list of things still to look at. Take one; if it is a pair you have not met, record its id first, then add its two parts to the list.
